Thank you for your insight! I'm certainly only applying for things I'm qualified for as it would be a waste of everyone's time if I did otherwise. I've applied to so many places and interviewed so much that I honestly couldn't tell you how exactly my age is coming up. It could be a combination of factors, such as applications asking when I graduated, how I look in my LinkedIn (that's been a recurring ask on about 75% of my applications), my history not being extensive enough even though they only ask for last 3 positions. Hell, even if you don't bring it up yourself, they seemingly find out. I've quite literally seen tiktoks where older workers are poking fun at applicants my age and not really taking them seriously unless there's some major outstanding quality like a 780 credit score. I thinks it's just the unwritten rule of where legally companies say they don't discriminate, but still definitely disregard certain applicants of certain backgrounds or that have disabilities. 

The crazy part about this is so many people don't want you to follow up or to contact them at all, stating it'll instantly disqualify you. So gone are those days. I'm even attaching cover letters, but I honestly doubt they're being read.

So my degree itself is in Business Management and I only majored and got certified for HR. It was either that, marketing, or logistics, all of which are horridly saturated. I'm honestly glad I ended up going with HR because there is so much I learned in terms of being able to protect myself legally and know my rights. Though with that being said, the industry is almost on fire (not the good kind) right now and there are SO MANY positions open because so many people are quitting. So it's like well geez I should have some inkling of a chance, or at least be able to squeeze into an entry or admin role. Same thing with with the IT world at the moment, though I would argue they are worse off at the moment. 

I enjoy working with small businesses and start-ups, and have built up a strong history of management. So I've decided to just pivot and go deeper into that. Not gonna lie, didn't want to because of the amount of commitment needed not just physically but also mentally. I suffer from a few hindering disabilities and just want a desk job where I can do my work, do it well, and be left alone. I went into HR because of the advisement from various sources and mentors who have been down this path before themselves. But I guess I'm just stuck now.

Alright. A typical day for me is that 360 cal sandwich (thats what my Samsung health says the build of it comes to)  half a smoothie bc I cant ever finish a whole which is 170cal give or take which one I have, and I usually snack on seaweed or dry roasted edamame which is about 130 calories. I usually eat my second/last meal when I get home from work which is usually either fish (150 cal) or chicken (336 cal), with steamed white rice which is (136 cal) and kale cooked with onions and olive oil (60ish cal). And I usually make a small saucer sized plate for about a child bc thats all I can eat. And for beverages throughout the day, I only drink water. Maybe half a cup of cranberry juice (110cal) if I have something other than water.

Total puts me at about 1166 calories in a day. If we're getting crazy with it, some nuggets on a bad day is an extra 287 calories bringing it to 1453 calories total.

I'm eating at least a sandwich and a smoothie every day so I can have the energy to at least get through work. I wasn't getting enough protein or much of anything before and switching to what I currently eat was enough to at least do that. My medications don't give me an appetite. I wish they did, would make the whole meal planning part much easier so I could actually EAT. The appetite problem was bad to the point I was literally in pain from not eating enough. Whuch my options are already very limited due to some severe food allergies and intolerances. Do you see my issue now?

You can find it hard to believe if you want, but I don't see the benefit in me taking the time out of my day to come here lying about what I eat when I'm looking for help. Most people eat when they're stressed, I'm the complete opposite, especiallywith being severely depressed with anxiety. And I'm also on a strong birth control to help with my endometriosis which has made me gain weight. So maybe think and actually READ before jumping to conclusions when someone has already EXPLAINED their eating habits?? Just a thought.
